channel.title: A Physically - Impossible Restraining Order
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "A Physically - Impossible Restraining Order" - physically limits how close one person can get to another

item.title: Re: A Physically - Impossible Restraining Order
item.content:encoded:
1) Don't provide hints; be obvious. Be as straightforward as possible.

2) "Central narrative" isn't how it will be presented, it's the story of the item in question. How you will be formatting is under the "Page Layout" section; we need to know the history of the item, and you haven't really provided anything. Sure, we know it's supposed to work, but we know nothing of the item itself. That's a major issue here.

3) All you've done under "Hook" is tell us more about formatting, and not why we should care about the item. In music, the hook is that initial riff that grabs someone and doesn't let go; There's none of that here. You've given a brief description of what it does and then nothing but formatting. We need a reason to care about this thing. Give us on!

item.title: Re: A Physically-Impossible Restraining Order
item.content:encoded:
(Don't think you need to be staff to critique)

But I don't really see how it would just be a basic test, this could be a very useful tool to the foundation (such as restricting certain PoIs from sites etc), so they'd work out all properties, such as, what if the distance was put at a very large distance (think to the sun), what if someone put everyone as the restrained person, its in all directions so what happens if someone is above someone when the document is filled out, could it be used to help espionage, etc. Also, you'd need at least 2 per test, apart from one where someone puts their name in put spots, for example.

item.title: Re: A Physically-Impossible Restraining Order
item.content:encoded:
Not a staff member but heres some criticism.

- A document that may be used to physically restrain someone
- If used, Person B would not be able to enter the distance provided by Person A for the stated amount of time.
- Person B is physically impended by an invisible barrier.

This is very confusing and needs more explanation.
This also needs to have more concepts because it's too basic as you can't really run any tests and should be just contained in a room where nobody can go through.

"The central narrative would be told over the testing logs, a baseline test to see how it works before certain "interesting" tests are done, the story here would be subtle in the notes afterwards, subjects reporting feeling safer after a certain death, etc."

What would they test with it? Just a single class D and just test how it works and they are done. I think its too basic to have multiple tests so yeah? They would already understand you just put names in and you can jail them for a space you put in.

"The testing logs will include what I believe to be unique testing logs, like what would happen if someone put their name in for both options, what would happen if the distance was set at a giant amount, etc."

They already know how it works so why would they continue to test it?

item.title: A Physically-Impossible Restraining Order
item.content:encoded:
A restraining order that physically limits how close one person can get to another

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard Format, Testing Logs.

Elevator Pitch:
- A document that may be used to physically restrain someone
- If used, Person B would not be able to enter the distance provided by Person A for the stated amount of time.
- Person B is physically impended by an invisible barrier.

Central Narrative:
The central narrative would be told over the testing logs, a baseline test to see how it works before certain "interesting" tests are done, the story here would be subtle in the notes afterwards, subjects reporting feeling safer after a certain death, etc.
Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The testing logs will include what I believe to be unique testing logs, like what would happen if someone put their name in for both options, what would happen if the distance was set at a giant amount, etc.
Additional Notes:
If people feel the story might not be clear just via notes of the testing logs, I might also include a discovery log which gives more hints (since I'd rather it not be obvious).
